description: Sustained active-prism renderer comparison and ABBA resource-recorder controls; synthetic GPU contention, not a game benchmark.

provenance.archive_note: Archive includes matching prism index.html, scene.js, scene.lua, wallpaper.json and Electron producer; preview.svg is omitted. The recorded scene hash covers the complete current prism directory including preview.svg. C/Rust edits made after archiving were not rebuilt for these captures.

setup.scanout: DP-2, AMD, approximately 144 Hz; helper presenter and contender render on NVIDIA RTX 4080.
setup.other_outputs: Other desktop outputs and pre-existing desktop wallpaper processes were left running.

case_names.idle: No prototype wallpaper assigned; daemon remains running.
case_names.chromium: Electron/Chromium SDR bitmap/copy producer and helper presenter; not the DMA-BUF path.

definitions.summary_arrays: [median of three run-level values, minimum, maximum]. Frames are not treated as independent benchmark repetitions.
definitions.cpu: Percent of one CPU core, summed by role. weighted_mean weights CPU-counter deltas by the actual sample interval. First synthetic zero sample is excluded; p99 uses linear interpolation over the remaining approximately 20 Hz samples. Wallpaper role includes the prototype daemon and assigned renderer process family. CPU is not total-system utilization. These are sampled fixed-process-set totals: process CPU clocks include exited threads within those sampled processes, but do not include separately spawned child processes absent from the set. Headline cpu_mean is the median of three time-weighted run means; headline cpu_p99 is the median of three per-run sample p99s.
definitions.presented_fps: Actual wp_presentation event count whose presentation timestamp lies inside the measured window, divided by full measured duration. This is one divided by duration higher than raw report presented_hz, which counts intervals.
definitions.presentation_ms: Intervals between consecutive actual presentation timestamps in the measured window, not frame callbacks, swap duration, or feedback receipt times. p99/p999 use linear interpolation; quantized intervals may interpolate to a value not observed in a frame.
definitions.sequence_gaps: Counts of differences in compositor output presentation sequence. For the 144 Hz contender, gap_ge2 means an update interval spanning at least two refreshes (~13.89 ms); gap_ge3 spans at least three (~20.83 ms). Percent denominator is consecutive presented intervals; per-minute denominator is measured wall duration. Wallpaper sequence gaps must be interpreted against its configured 30 fps cadence.
definitions.excess_refreshes: Sum of max(sequence_gap - 1, 0), scaled per minute; distinct from gap event count and discarded feedback.
definitions.severe_clusters: Contender intervals with sequence gap >=3 or interval >50 ms. Merge successive event end timestamps when separated by <=100 ms. Cluster duration is last event end minus first event end; a single event has duration zero.
definitions.periodicity: Exploratory 100 ms event-count bins, autocorrelation over 0.2-10 s; phase coherence at selected periods. Nonstationary clusters and sparse events can create peaks. No multiple-testing correction or causal conclusion.
definitions.near_event_cpu: Descriptive CPU-sample means within +/-50 ms of severe contender event end times versus other samples. Temporal association is not causal attribution.
definitions.gpu_command_ms: Asynchronous helper GL timer query. Native wallpaper covers its helper scene and draw work; Chromium helper timing excludes Chromium producer rendering, readback and IPC. Global NVIDIA utilization is coarsely averaged and not per-process or millisecond attribution.
definitions.cpu_submit_wall_ms: Elapsed helper rendering/submission/swap wall time, not consumed CPU time.
definitions.browser_callback_telemetry: Cumulative callback frame delta divided by telemetry date delta; unique date batches used for interval summaries. Callback cadence is not proof of visible presentation. Baseline WebKit has no actual wallpaper-presentation trace.
definitions.recorder_off: Disables resource sampling and one-second API polling; buffered helper frame logging stays enabled. CPU and sampler measurements are null, not zero.
definitions.paired_comparisons: Engine minus comparator with matching repetition number. values are repetition 1, 2, 3; median_range is [median, minimum, maximum]. CPU deltas are percentage points of one core; gap percentages are percentage-point differences.

video_audio_screening.asset_note: Ancillary asset manifest records tide MP4/SVG/HTML/Lua/manifest, runtime JavaScript, and the native Electron addon. The supplemental archive preserves the referenced asset bundle.
video_audio_screening.design: One 90-second measured tide video/audio run per renderer after 20-second warmup; a separate screening pass, not three repetitions per renderer.
video_audio_screening.metric_scope: CPU numbers are each single run's time-weighted mean and per-run 20 Hz sample p99, not medians across repeats. Actual FPS is presentation count / duration. Browser callback cadence is distinct.
findings: All three screening runs are valid. Measured wallpaper CPU mean/p99 (% one core): WebKit 104.63/124.92, Lua/OpenGL 3.22/6.27, Chromium SDR copy 55.04/90.52.
Contender actual presentation rates: WebKit 137.83/s, Lua/OpenGL 142.94/s, Chromium SDR copy 140.54/s. Gap >=2 refresh rates are 324.67, 57.33, 201.33 per minute; >=3 rates are 44, 6, 6 per minute.

Lua/OpenGL wallpaper presents at 30.00/s, p99 interval 41.668 ms; Chromium wallpaper presents at 25.16/s, p99 interval 69.448 ms, while its browser callbacks are 30/s. WebKit callbacks average 23.28/s; its actual display rate is not instrumented.
Native telemetry reports hwdec=nvdec in all 90 observations, directly supporting native hardware decoder selection. Browser hardware decode is not established by the recorded browser telemetry.

WebKit and Chromium browser video telemetry reports 1280x720, duration 8 seconds, readyState 4, no errors and unpaused playback in all 90 polls; playback positions change. Audio is available without errors in all browser polls; RMS changes, and the native helper has varying audio RMS.
caveats: No matched idle run or audio-off pass. Do not subtract main prism results to claim an isolated video or audio cost, or present this one-pass screening as equivalent replication.
Hardware decoder selection and changing playback position do not establish AV synchronization, decode drop rate, end-to-end latency or HDR correctness.
Global NVIDIA decoder utilization includes unrelated desktop video activity; it cannot establish which browser used hardware decoding.
Native helper GPU timer scope excludes asynchronous decoding; its very small video query time is not total video decode/render GPU cost.
The common frozen-process CPU accounting and coarse resource-sampling limitations still apply.

browser_callback_telemetry.note: The one retained telemetry date and its interval array predate the paused measurement; they are not fresh paused-frame timing. Frame counters remain unchanged across all 60 polls.
The one retained telemetry date and its interval array predate the paused measurement; they are not fresh paused-frame timing. Frame counters remain unchanged across all 60 polls.

paused_screening.design: One 60-second measured paused-prism run per renderer after 20-second warmup; separate screening pass, not repeated paired active/paused trials.
paused_screening.metric_scope: Each CPU mean is time-weighted over its single run; p99 is that run's approximately 20 Hz sample p99. No median-of-repeats or main-run pairing.
findings: All three runs pass capture validity checks and report the wallpaper surface paused in 60/60 polls.
Measured wallpaper CPU mean/p99 (% one core): WebKit 0.430/2.821, Lua/OpenGL 0.384/2.801, Chromium SDR copy 2.267/5.486. Chromium still has measurable residual CPU while scene frames stop.
Lua/OpenGL and Chromium helper traces contain zero actual wallpaper presentations in the 60-second measured window; helper frame counters are unchanged (67 and 56 respectively).

WebKit scene frame counter stays at 47 and Chromium browser scene frame counter at 82 in every poll. Their telemetry dates are frozen and retained interval arrays are stale; no fresh callback timing samples exist. WebKit actual display presentation remains uninstrumented.

Contender actual presentation rates: WebKit-paused 143.15/s, Lua-paused 142.05/s, Chromium-paused 142.93/s. Gap >=2 refresh rates are 47, 113, 64 per minute; >=3 rates are 3, 2, 0 per minute. Low paused CPU is not proof that all host presentation gaps disappear.
caveats: No concurrent or same-pass idle measurement and no repeated randomized active/paused pairs; do not interpret differences from main active runs as an isolated causal pause effect.
This is a configured pause check with SDR prism and audio disabled. It does not establish fullscreen detection latency, audio/video suspension, hotplug behavior or compositor occlusion policy.
Frozen scene callback counters do not prove that browser internal timers, IPC, housekeeping or all GPU work stopped.
Capture hashes refer to the historical binaries used for this run. Subsequent reviewed source edits/rebuilds are outside the recorded comparison.
Common fixed-process CPU accounting and coarse resource-attribution limitations still apply.

final_build_screening.design: One 60-second measured run each of idle, Lua/OpenGL prism and Chromium SDR copy prism after 20-second warmup; final rebuilt helper/daemon/producer, separate screening from the historical repeated comparison.
final_build_screening.metric_scope: Each CPU weighted_mean and p99 describes one final-build run. No three-run median or formal equivalence test is available for this build. Actual presentation FPS uses event count / measured duration.

provenance_checks.note: These checks refer to files immediately after this final-build screening; the earlier 22 captures retain their original identities.

findings: All three final-build captures are valid; source scene hash matches historical prism, while presenter, daemon and Electron producer hashes differ.
Measured wallpaper CPU mean/p99 (% one core): idle 0.210/2.334, Lua/OpenGL 1.243/4.268, Chromium SDR copy 54.549/95.945. The low-native/high-browser CPU ordering remains.

Contender presentation in this final-build pass: idle 143.816 fps with 11 >=2-refresh gaps/min; Lua/OpenGL 139.250 fps with 285/min; Chromium 143.983 fps with zero gaps. No >=3-refresh contender gaps occur in any of these minutes.

Lua versus same-pass idle loses 4.567 contender fps and adds 274 >=2-refresh gaps/min. This is worse ordinary contender cadence than any historical Lua run (141.417-143.400 fps, 33-133 gaps/min), although its severe tail does not worsen in this short window.

Chromium versus same-pass idle is 0.167 contender fps higher with 11 fewer >=2-refresh gaps/min. Its actual wallpaper presentation remains poor: 21.183 fps despite 30.001 browser callbacks/s, with wallpaper p99 interval 104.171 ms.
Final-build relative contender cadence differs from the historical repeated result; the historical near-idle native behavior must not be carried forward as final-build assurance.
caveats: One serial 60-second run per case, not a repeated randomized comparison. No WebKit final-build case and no final-build recorder ABBA controls were captured.

The helper, daemon and producer changed, and the helper also runs the contender. Cross-build contender changes therefore combine harness/workload implementation changes and scene behavior with uncontrolled host variation; do not attribute them to the wallpaper renderer alone.

Contemporaneous compositor CPU differs materially: mean 31.69% of one core at final idle, 30.65% with Lua, 53.27% with Chromium. Global NVIDIA decode utilization also varies despite audio/video being disabled in the tested prism wallpaper, reflecting other desktop activity. Neither fact identifies a cause.

Zero severe gaps in one minute is a short-window observation, not a bound on rare hitches. Native's ordinary-gap increase warrants sustained repeated measurement before claiming final-build gameplay suitability.
Wallpaper callback and actual presentation rates remain different; Chromium's good contender trace does not establish smooth wallpaper delivery.

Common frozen-process CPU membership, coarse NVML integration, 20 Hz CPU resolution, cross-GPU scanout and synthetic-workload limitations remain. Earlier measurements and hashes are retained unchanged.

recorder_controls.design: ABBA: off1, on1, on2, off2; 60 s measured plus 20 s warmup; idle wallpaper case, 600-pass 144 fps contender; settings and hashes match main except duration/repeats and recorder state.
recorder_controls.conclusion: Recorder used about 0.61% of one core in enabled idle controls; no consistent added presentation penalty. Apparent mean benefit comes from noisier off2. One isolated three-refresh event occurred in on2. This controls resource/API sampling overhead, not buffered frame logging or active renderer-specific telemetry overhead.

findings: WebKit reduces contender FPS and increases >=2-refresh and >=3-refresh gap rates versus same-repeat idle in all three repetitions.

Lua/OpenGL has measured CPU use of about 0.92% of one CPU core and delivers about 30 actual wallpaper presentations/s. Contender change versus idle reverses direction across repetitions; the second native run has a worse severe tail, so hitch-free equivalence is not established.

Chromium SDR copy has measured CPU use of about 50% of one core, improves contender presentation versus WebKit, but is consistently worse than idle. Its JS callbacks stay at 30/s while actual wallpaper presentation is 21.29-24.74/s, with wallpaper intervals up to 104.17 ms.
Both alternatives reduce >=2-refresh contender gap rates versus WebKit in all repetitions. Native has a worse >=3-refresh rate than WebKit in repetition 2 despite a higher overall FPS.
No contender interval exceeds 50 ms; worst is about 27.78 ms. Such intervals still span four refreshes at 144 Hz.

Hitches cluster irregularly, including idle. A roughly 3 s exploratory severe-event autocorrelation peak occurs in Chromium repetitions 1 and 3, but is not replicated in repetition 2; no stable periodic cause is established.
caveats: Three serial two-minute repetitions per case with reversed order only in repetition 2; no randomized replication, confidence interval or formal equivalence test.

One active SDR prism wallpaper on DP-2, audio disabled, fixed synthetic 1280x720 600-pass GPU workload at 144 fps. These results do not establish behavior in a game, at saturation, paused/fullscreen, HDR, video/audio, multiple wallpaper outputs or the Chromium DMA-BUF path.
The compared renderer implementations differ and delivered wallpaper cadences differ. This is end-to-end prototype behavior at equal configured FPS, not equal-output-work engine efficiency.
Cross-GPU NVIDIA rendering and AMD scanout plus ongoing compositor/desktop processes limit generalization and attribution.

Process-family membership is frozen after warmup and checked for surviving new descendants at run end. A child process created and exited between snapshots can evade both CPU accounting and the final membership check. Such missing CPU does not invalidate independently recorded presentation/cadence. The archived daemon uses direct Hyprland Unix-socket IPC, so a recurring daemon hyprctl subprocess is not evidenced in this captured source.
Recorder cost varies with active renderer: median means about 0.61%, 0.87%, 0.68%, 1.23% of one core for idle, WebKit, native, Chromium. ABBA controls cover idle recorder overhead only.

Global NVML polling is around 4.3 Hz in these runs with native integration windows around 1/6-1 second; the 20 Hz CPU sampler cannot resolve a 7 ms scheduling cause. AMD GPU, runqueue delay and per-process GPU counters are absent.
All timestamps used for presentation comparisons are CLOCK_MONOTONIC; feedback receipt can arrive milliseconds later and must not be substituted for display time.
Raw verification artifacts remain local and ignored. This sanitized summary contains relative paths and no usernames, process IDs, monitor serials or original wallpaper assignments.
